title: First ancient human genome (Saqqaq man)
summary: Scientists sequenced nearly 80% of the genome of a Paleo-Eskimo man of the Saqqaq culture from 4,000-year-old hair found in Greenland. It pointed to a separate migration from Siberia about 5,500 years ago.
why: Opened the era of reading whole genomes of ancient people.

notes.problem: Wrong place: the 2010 genome paper says the hair was 'recovered from Qeqertasussuk, Greenland', not Qeqertarsuaq on Disko Island (cited page says only 'found in Greenland').
Qeqertasussuk and 'related to peoples of northeastern Siberia' are not in the source; source gives Greenland, nearly 80%, and a separate Siberian migration about 5,500 years ago.

superlativeSource: the first genome sequencing of an ancient human
